We adopt a high-frequency oscillation-based initialization combined with adaptive local optimization to address the nonconvexity and high dimensionality of the problem. This approach leverages the fact that signals with high-frequency components exhibit reduced correlation with their shifted versions due to minimal temporal overlap. By constructing an initial guess through inverse Fourier Transform (IFT) of a carefully designed spectrum with dominant high-frequency energy, we bias the search toward solutions with minimal overlap properties. The optimization phase then refines this structured initialization with gradient-based local search, ensuring both constraint satisfaction and objective minimization. This differs from prior strategies by focusing on spectral characteristics rather than arbitrary pattern templates.

Let h: [0,2] → [0,1] be the step function with n_points samples. We represent h as a discrete-time signal with the constraint:
